+\begin{abstract}
+We study one-position overlap chains of bounded representations of zero in a
+fixed Pisot linear numeration system.  If $U=(u_j)$ is strictly increasing,
+$u_0=1$, and its recurrence has a nonintegral Pisot characteristic root,
+then for every fixed coefficient bound $D$ there is an effective constant
+$C(U,D)$.  Unless a nonzero overlap chain reaches a directed cycle, its
+transient has fewer than $C(U,D)m$ edges at aperture $m$.  The proof uses an
+arbitrary-alphabet adjacent-collapse lemma: contracting conjugates force the
+second quotient in two consecutive zero representations to vanish and fix
+the newly exposed coefficient.  No Condition~F or zero-preservation
+hypothesis is required.
+
+As an exact application, consider the cyclic rank recoding obtained by
+extending the canonical rank of legal length-$m$ words to the full digit
+cube and reducing it modulo $u_m$.  Its coordinatewise-difference graph is
+exactly the bounded-zero overlap graph for the canonical difference
+alphabet.  Hence injectivity implies an aperture-linear future-only inverse
+depth.  A fixed binary cubic recurrence with leading root of
+$x^3-2x^2+x-1$ attains the linear order: for every $m\ge4$ its cyclic rank
+recoding is injective and has exact causal length
+$2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-1$.  We classify the penultimate obstruction set as
+$\{E_m,-E_m\}$ and prove that the next set is empty.  The same words show
+that the bounded-zero transient bound itself has sharp linear order.
+\end{abstract}
+
+\medskip
+\noindent{\bf 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification.}
+Primary: 37B10, 11B39; Secondary: 11A67, 37B40.
+
+\medskip
+\noindent{\bf Key words and phrases.}
+Pisot numeration, bounded representation of zero, overlap graph, linear
+transient, cyclic rank recoding, future-only inverse, collision quotient.

+\section{Introduction}
+\label{sec:introduction}
+
+Bounded representations of zero are a standard finite-state object in
+Pisot numeration.  Their regularity supports normalization and arithmetic
+algorithms, but regularity by itself does not control how long an
+aperture-dependent chain of overlapping zero representations can remain
+transient.  We consider the following narrow quantitative question.  Fix a
+Pisot recurrence $U=(u_j)$ and a coefficient alphabet $[-D,D]\cap\mathbb Z$.
+At aperture $m$, use a length-$m$ coefficient word as a state transition
+exactly when it can be completed by a coefficient of the distinguished
+weight $u_m$ to represent zero.  Consecutive edges overlap by one position.
+How long can a path beginning with an exposed nonzero coefficient survive if
+it never reaches a cycle?
+
+Our first main result, Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient}, gives
+an effective linear answer.  There is a computable $C(U,D)<\infty$ such that
+every such transient has fewer than $C(U,D)m$ edges.  Equivalently, after a
+nonzero chain is anchored at its first exposed nonzero coefficient, it
+either enters a repeatable periodic tail or has only linearly many further
+overlaps.  The coefficient completing an edge is not assumed to belong to
+$[-D,D]$; it is proved to lie in a fixed interval
+$[-K_{U,D},K_{U,D}]$.  This mixed-alphabet point is essential to the correct
+edge formulation.
+
+The mechanism is local.  Lemma
+\ref{lem:bounded-zero-arbitrary-alphabet-collapse} compares two consecutive
+zero representations under every algebraic embedding.  The contracting
+conjugates bound the nondominant sums, while a finite exact separation in the
+dominant embedding prevents any nonzero value of
+$e_{t+m}+k_t-\beta k_{t+1}$ once $m$ is large enough.  Irrationality then
+forces
+\[
+k_{t+1}=0,\qquad e_{t+m}=-k_t.
+\]
+Along a path, every quotient after the first vanishes and all later appended
+coefficients vanish after one exceptional position.  A path of $m+1$ edges
+therefore reaches the zero state, which already has a loop.  The finitely
+many smaller apertures are handled by exact acyclic longest-path searches.
+This gives an effective constant without counting all
+$(2D+1)^{m-1}$ states.
+
+The proof requires neither Condition~F nor preservation of leading zeros.
+Finite-state recognition of bounded zero representations in Pisot systems is
+classical \cite{Frougny1992}, and recent work places zero preservation in a
+precise Condition~F framework \cite{CartonSudberyYassawi2026}.  Those results
+do not imply an aperture-linear survival bound for the moving overlap graphs
+considered here.  Conversely, our result does not assert finite expansion,
+normalization complexity, or a general synchronization theorem.  The
+distinguished terminal weight $u_m$ and consecutive recurrence weights are
+part of the statement.
+
+The second part applies the standard-object theorem to a symbolic recoding.
+For a strictly increasing Pisot numeration system, order the legal
+length-$m$ words by canonical rank, extend the same positional rank to the
+full digit cube, reduce it modulo the number $u_m$ of legal words, and return
+the legal word with that residue.  Overlap these recoded windows along the
+shift.  We call the resulting factor code a cyclic language-rank recoding.
+It is a congruence of integer language ranks, not numerical
+$\beta$-normalization in $\mathbb Z[\beta]$.
+
+Lemma~\ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient} proves that the
+coordinatewise-difference quotient of the pair graph loses no collision:
+every bounded digit difference is realized by its positive and negative
+parts.  The quotient is exactly the graph $G_m(U,d_U)$ from the first part.
+The longest path from a first-coordinate-nonzero state is exactly one less
+than the least future-only inverse window, and injectivity is equivalent to
+the absence of a reachable cycle.  Corollary
+\ref{cor:pisot-linear-causal-depth} therefore gives
+\[
+\Phi_{U,m}\text{ injective}
+\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le C_Um. \tag{A1}
+\]
+This is a consequence of the bounded-zero theorem and the exact quotient,
+not the definitional center of the argument.
+
+Classical pair and fiber graphs supply reachable-cycle tests and finite
+inverse windows for injective local maps
+\cite{AmorosoPatt1972,Richardson1972,Nasu1977,Head1989,LindMarcus1995,
+Nasu1995}.  Their generic state-count bound is exponential in $m$ here.
+Likewise, Ashley's decoder-window estimates are linear in the number of
+states of a presenting graph, not in this aperture
+\cite{Ashley1988,Ashley1996}.  The bounded-delay theorem of
+Frougny and Sakarovitch starts from a rational relation already known to have
+bounded delay; it does not derive an $O(m)$ delay from injectivity
+\cite{FrougnySakarovitch1991}.  The arithmetic adjacent-collapse lemma is
+what changes the scale from exponential to linear.
+
+Finally, Theorem~\ref{thm:fixed-cubic-sharpness} proves sharpness inside one
+fixed system.  Let $\theta$ be the leading root of
+$x^3-2x^2+x-1$ and use the binary recurrence beginning $1,2,4$.  For every
+$m\ge4$,
+\[
+\Phi_{\theta,m}\text{ is injective},\qquad
+\ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)=2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-1. \tag{A2}
+\]
+The proof classifies the penultimate obstruction set exactly as
+$\{E_m,-E_m\}$ and the next obstruction set as empty.  Read only as bounded
+coefficient words, the same $E_m$ give paths of length at least $m-3$ in
+$G_m(U_\theta,1)$.  One object therefore proves sharpness both for the
+inverse-depth corollary and for the bounded-zero transient theorem.
+
+The article is organized in this logical order.  Section
+\ref{sec:bounded-zero-transients} defines the overlap chains, proves the
+arbitrary-alphabet collapse lemma, and proves the linear transient theorem.
+Section~\ref{sec:cyclic-rank-application} introduces cyclic ranks, proves the
+exact collision quotient, and deduces \textup{(A1)}.  Section
+\ref{sec:fixed-cubic-sharpness} proves \textup{(A2)}--\textup{(A3)} and the
+terminal classification.  Section~\ref{sec:comparative-context} records the
+limited comparison with the family-classification problem.  The companion
+article by the present authors, \emph{Exact overlap thresholds and
+future-only inverse depth for cyclic ranks of quadratic and simple-Parry
+beta-languages}, contains the full Fibonacci, quadratic, and simple-Parry
+classification.

-If each output word is relabeled by its canonical rank in
-$\mathbb Z/u_m\mathbb Z$, the local rule is
-\[
-(x_0,\ldots,x_{m-1})\longmapsto

-\]
-Thus the word-valued rule is a symbolwise bijective relabeling of a modular
-weighted sliding block code.  The weights, the modulus $u_m$, and their
-variation with $m$ are specific to the present family.  This is not a linear
-cellular automaton: in general $D_U$ is only a digit subset of
-$\mathbb Z/u_m\mathbb Z$, not a module on which the rule is a group

-The scope is not a disguised standard-initial-value convention.  For
-example, standard $k$-bonacci initial conditions begin $1,1,\ldots$ and fail
-strict increase, whereas the customary shift beginning $1,2,\ldots$ belongs
-to the present class.  Nor do we assume Condition~F: that would be a genuine
-restriction, since the principal root of $x^3-3x^2+2x-1$ is Pisot but does
-not satisfy Condition~F \cite[Theorem~3]{Akiyama2000}.  The equivalence of
-Condition~F with zero preservation is proved in
-\cite{CartonSudberyYassawi2026}, but neither property is used below.

-\begin{lemma}[Exact collision quotient for $U$]

-\begin{proof}
-Two folded windows agree exactly when the difference of their raw values is
-divisible by $u_m$, because the canonical normal words represent
-$0,\ldots,u_m-1$ bijectively.  Every $e\in\Delta_U$ is realized as a
-difference of two digits by taking its positive and negative parts in

-\begin{theorem}[Fixed-base linear causal depth and sharpness for Pisot numeration]
-\label{thm:pisot-linear-depth-sharpness}
-Let $U$ be any strictly increasing Pisot numeration system with $u_0=1$,

-\end{equation*}

-reach a directed cycle, every directed path from that initial state set has

-\begin{corollary}[Global overlap dichotomy for bounded zero representations]
-\label{cor:pisot-zero-strip-synchronization}
-For a fixed strictly increasing Pisot numeration $U$ as in the theorem and an
-aperture $m\ge2$,
-consider all bounded zero words of length $m+1$ of the form
+The coefficient $c$ completing an edge is unique and satisfies
+$|c|\le K_{U,D}$: uniqueness follows from $u_m>0$, and
 \[
-[e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0
+|c|\le D\frac{\sum_{j<m}u_j}{u_m}
+ <\frac{DA_U}{b_U(\beta-1)}.

-which overlap one digit at a time.  Each row is a standard bounded
-$U$-representation of zero; only its organization into this one-position
-overlap chain is specific here.  Exactly one of the following global
-alternatives holds: some chain with a nonzero coefficient has a finite prefix
-followed by a periodic bounded zero representation; or every nonzero chain
-has fewer than $(C_U+1)m$ rows.  The latter bound has sharp order $\Theta(m)$
-for $U_\theta$.
-\end{corollary}

-\begin{proof}
-The overlapping rows are exactly paths in $\Gamma_{U,m}$ by
-\eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}.  A cycle reachable from $B_{U,m}$ gives
-the first alternative by repeating the cycle.  If no such cycle is
-reachable, \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1} bounds every path from $B_{U,m}$.
-Unless a chain is zero, at most $m-1$ initial shifts pass before one of its
-nonzero coordinates occupies the first position, after which fewer than
-$C_Um$ further rows are possible.  The two alternatives are mutually
-exclusive because the periodic tail makes chains arbitrarily long.  The
-words $E_m$ in \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3} give the matching lower order for
-$U_\theta$.
-\end{proof}

+The theorem also gives the useful global chain dichotomy.  Consider all
+bounded zero words of length $m+1$ that overlap one digit at a time.  Either
+some chain with a nonzero coefficient has a finite prefix followed by a
+periodic bounded zero representation, or every nonzero chain has fewer than
+$(C(U,D)+1)m$ rows.  Indeed, a reachable cycle gives the periodic tail.  In
+the absence of such a cycle, at most $m-1$ initial shifts pass before a
+nonzero coordinate occupies the first position, after which the theorem
+bounds the remaining overlaps.  The alternatives are mutually exclusive
+because a periodic tail can be repeated to make arbitrarily long chains.

-terminal word for aperture $m-1$ followed by zero, namely $\pm E_m$.
-With one more row the terminal four-digit alternatives are
-\eqref{eq:theta-four-tail-table}; now $m-5$ has even parity and its forced
-zero propagates to $e_0$.  Hence the next obstruction set is empty.
-
-For $m=4,5$, successive exact division in the two or three window
-congruences gives
-\[
-\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
-m&Q_m&\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m-1}
-&\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}\\ \hline
-4&12&\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1)\}&\varnothing\\
-5&21&\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1,0)\}&\varnothing.
-\end{array}
-\]
-This is an exhaustive integer calculation: in each row the quotient is in
-$\{-1,0,1\}$ by \eqref{eq:theta-carry-one}, and the last digit determines
-the preceding bounded digit successively.  Thus \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3}
-holds for every $m\ge4$.  Lemma
-\ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient} now gives
-\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A2}, including injectivity, and the limiting statement
-is immediate.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Global overlap dichotomy for bounded zero representations]
-\label{cor:pisot-zero-strip-synchronization}
-For a fixed strictly increasing Pisot numeration $U$ as in the theorem and an
-aperture $m\ge2$,
-consider all bounded zero words of length $m+1$ of the form
-\[
-[e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0
-\]
-which overlap one digit at a time.  Each row is a standard bounded
-$U$-representation of zero; only its organization into this one-position
-overlap chain is specific here.  Exactly one of the following global
-alternatives holds: some chain with a nonzero coefficient has a finite prefix
-followed by a periodic bounded zero representation; or every nonzero chain
-has fewer than $(C_U+1)m$ rows.  The latter bound has sharp order $\Theta(m)$
-for $U_\theta$.
 \end{corollary}
 
 \begin{proof}
-The overlapping rows are exactly paths in $\Gamma_{U,m}$ by
-\eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}.  A cycle reachable from $B_{U,m}$ gives
-the first alternative by repeating the cycle.  If no such cycle is
-reachable, \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1} bounds every path from $B_{U,m}$.
-Unless a chain is zero, at most $m-1$ initial shifts pass before one of its
-nonzero coordinates occupies the first position, after which fewer than
-$C_Um$ further rows are possible.  The two alternatives are mutually
-exclusive because the periodic tail makes chains arbitrarily long.  The
-words $E_m$ in \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3} give the matching lower order for
-$U_\theta$.
-\end{proof}
-
-We now detach the contraction argument from the canonical digit-difference
-alphabet.  Fix $D\ge1$ and retain the effective Binet and growth data in
-\eqref{eq:pisot-binet}--\eqref{eq:pisot-effective-growth}.  Put
-\begin{equation}
-K_{U,D}=\left\lceil\frac{DA_U}{b_U(\beta-1)}\right\rceil
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-carry-bound}
-\end{equation}
-and
-\begin{equation}
-\delta_{U,D}=\min\left\{|a+k-\beta l|:
- |a|\le D,\ |k|,|l|\le K_{U,D},\ a+k-\beta l\ne0\right\}.
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-separation}
-\end{equation}
-The variables in this minimum are integers.  Since $\beta$ is irrational,
-$\delta_{U,D}>0$, and exact algebraic-number comparison computes it.  Define
-\begin{align}
-M_{U,D}&=\frac1{c_0}\sum_{i=1}^{s-1}|c_i|
- \left(\frac{D}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_{U,D}\right),\nonumber\\
-B_{U,D}&=D+(1+\beta)M_{U,D},
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-conjugate-bound}
-\end{align}
-and
-\begin{equation}
-m_0(U,D)=\min\{m\ge2:\beta^m\delta_{U,D}>B_{U,D}\}.
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-contraction-threshold}
-\end{equation}
-All these constants are effective from $U$ and $D$.

-\begin{lemma}[Adjacent collapse for an arbitrary bounded coefficient alphabet]
-\label{lem:bounded-zero-arbitrary-alphabet-collapse}
-Let $U$ satisfy the integral recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is
-the minimal polynomial of a nonintegral Pisot number $\beta$, and fix
-$D\ge1$.  If $m\ge m_0(U,D)$, coefficients
-$e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m}\in[-D,D]\cap\mathbb Z$, and integers $k_t,k_{t+1}$
-satisfy
-\[
-\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_je_{t+j}=k_tu_m,
-\qquad
-\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_je_{t+1+j}=k_{t+1}u_m,
-\]
-then
-\[
-k_{t+1}=0,\qquad e_{t+m}=-k_t.
-\]
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The growth bounds give, for either row,
-\[
-|k_t|\le D\frac{\sum_{j<m}u_j}{u_m}
- <\frac{DA_U}{b_U(\beta-1)}\le K_{U,D},
-\]
-and similarly $|k_{t+1}|\le K_{U,D}$.  For every embedding set
-\[
-A_{t,i}=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}e_{t+j}\beta_i^j-k_t\beta_i^m.
-\]
-The recurrence and its Binet expansion give $\sum_i c_iA_{t,i}=0$.
-For $i\ge1$,
-\[
-|A_{t,i}|\le\frac{D}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_{U,D},
-\]
-so $|A_{t,0}|\le M_{U,D}$, and the same holds at $t+1$.
-Direct subtraction of the adjacent dominant-embedding sums gives the exact
-identity
-\begin{equation}
-\beta^m(e_{t+m}+k_t-\beta k_{t+1})
-=\beta A_{t+1,0}-A_{t,0}+e_t.
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-adjacent-identity}
-\end{equation}
-The right side has modulus at most $B_{U,D}$.  If the parenthesis on the
-left were nonzero, \eqref{eq:bounded-zero-separation} and
-\eqref{eq:bounded-zero-contraction-threshold} would make the left side
-strictly larger than $B_{U,D}$, a contradiction.  Hence
-$e_{t+m}+k_t=\beta k_{t+1}$.  Irrationality of $\beta$ and integrality of
-the three coefficients force $k_{t+1}=0$ and $e_{t+m}=-k_t$.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Linear transient bound for bounded $U$-representations of zero]
-\label{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient}
-Let $U=(u_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
-with $u_0=1$, satisfying the integral recurrence whose characteristic
-polynomial is the minimal polynomial of a nonintegral Pisot number $\beta$.
-Fix $D\ge1$.  For $m\ge2$, let $G_m(U,D)$ be the directed graph with vertex
-set
-\[
-([-D,D]\cap\mathbb Z)^{m-1}.
-\]
-There is an edge
-\[
-(e_0,\ldots,e_{m-2})\longrightarrow
-(e_1,\ldots,e_{m-2},e_{m-1})
-\]
-if and only if there is an integer $c$ such that
-\begin{equation}
-e_0u_0+e_1u_1+\cdots+e_{m-1}u_{m-1}+cu_m=0.
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-overlap-edge}
-\end{equation}
-The completing coefficient is unique and necessarily satisfies
-$|c|\le K_{U,D}$.
-Then there is an effectively computable $C(U,D)<\infty$ such that, for every
-$m\ge2$, if no directed cycle of $G_m(U,D)$ is reachable from a vertex whose
-first coordinate is nonzero, every directed path beginning at such a vertex
-has fewer than $C(U,D)m$ edges.
-
-Equivalently, after shifting a chain so that its initial exposed coefficient
-is nonzero, either it reaches a directed cycle, or it has fewer than
-$C(U,D)m$ further overlaps.  The graphs are finite-state recognizers of these
-overlap chains, and their edges are bounded $U$-representations of zero by
-\eqref{eq:bounded-zero-overlap-edge}.
-
-The linear order is sharp.  For the fixed recurrence
-\[
-u_0=1,\quad u_1=2,\quad u_2=4,\qquad
-u_{n+3}=2u_{n+2}-u_{n+1}+u_n,
-\]
-whose leading root is the Pisot root of $x^3-2x^2+x-1$, and for $D=1$, the
-maximum finite path length is at least $m-3$ for every $m\ge4$.
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-For an edge at time $t$, write $k_t=-c$ in
-\eqref{eq:bounded-zero-overlap-edge}.  The growth estimate gives
-$|k_t|\le K_{U,D}$ uniformly in $m$.  Suppose first that
-$m\ge m_0(U,D)$.  Along any path of at least two edges, Lemma
-\ref{lem:bounded-zero-arbitrary-alphabet-collapse}, applied to each adjacent
-pair, gives
-\[
-k_1=k_2=\cdots=0,\qquad
-e_m=-k_0,\qquad e_{m+1}=e_{m+2}=\cdots=0.
-\]
-A path of $m+1$ edges therefore reaches the all-zero vertex.  That vertex
-has a loop, so such a path would make a directed cycle reachable from its
-initial vertex.  Under the hypothesis of the theorem, every path has at
-most $m$ edges for $m\ge m_0(U,D)$.
-
-For each of the finitely many $2\le m<m_0(U,D)$, the graph is finite.  When
-no cycle is reachable from the first-coordinate-nonzero vertices, exact
-acyclic longest-path search computes the maximum $p_{U,D}(m)$; set it to
-zero otherwise.  Thus, for example,
-\[
-C(U,D)=\max\left(2,
- \max_{2\le m<m_0(U,D)}
- \left\lceil\frac{1+p_{U,D}(m)}m\right\rceil\right)
-\]
-is effective and has the required property, with the inner maximum understood
-as zero when $m_0(U,D)=2$.
-
-For sharpness, the coefficient words $E_m$ in
-\eqref{eq:theta-terminal-word} satisfy the integer recurrence relations
-classified in \eqref{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization}--
-\eqref{eq:theta-five-tail-table}.  Read only as coefficient words, they give
-paths in $G_m(U,1)$ of length
-$2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-2\ge m-3$.  The next bounded-coefficient path set is
-empty by the same exact terminal calculation, so no reachable cycle occurs.
-This conclusion uses the recurrence identities alone, independently of any
-realization of the coefficients as differences of raw words.
+If the Pisot root has degree one, then $u_j=b^j$,
+$D_U=\{0,\ldots,b-1\}$, the fold is the identity, and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)=1$; take $C_U=1$.  Otherwise apply
+Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient} with $D=d_U$.  Its graph is
+exactly $\Gamma_{U,m}$, because \eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge} is the
+edge condition \eqref{eq:bounded-zero-overlap-edge-theorem}.  By Lemma
+\ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient}, injectivity is equivalent to the
+absence of a reachable cycle and the causal length is one plus the longest
+path length.  Since the theorem gives fewer than $C(U,d_U)m$ edges, the
+integer path length is at most $C(U,d_U)m-1$.  Taking
+$C_U=C(U,d_U)$ proves both formulations.
 \end{proof}
 
-\begin{remark}[Logical boundary of the standard-object theorem]
-\label{rem:bounded-zero-standard-object-boundary}
-The statement and proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient}
-use only a fixed Pisot recurrence, bounded integer coefficients, the
-distinguished weight $u_m$, and one-position overlaps of bounded
-$U$-representations of zero.  They use no canonical rank bijection, legal-word
-alphabet, cyclic reduction map, positive/negative realization of
-coefficients, image shift, or inverse decoder.  The distinguished modulus
-$u_m$ and consecutive recurrence weights remain essential: replacing $u_m$
-by an unrelated modulus destroys \eqref{eq:bounded-zero-adjacent-identity}.
-The theorem therefore does not concern numerical $\beta$-normalization,
-successor carry propagation, general synchronized transductions, general
-right-closing maps, or a broad class of sliding block codes.
-\end{remark}
+The scope is not a disguised standard-initial-value convention.  For
+example, standard $k$-bonacci initial conditions begin $1,1,\ldots$ and fail
+strict increase, whereas the customary shift beginning $1,2,\ldots$ belongs
+to the present class.  Nor is Condition~F assumed: the principal root of
+$x^3-3x^2+2x-1$ is Pisot but does not satisfy Condition~F
+\cite[Theorem~3]{Akiyama2000}.  The equivalence of Condition~F with zero
+preservation is proved in \cite{CartonSudberyYassawi2026}, but neither
+property enters the corollary.

-\begin{lemma}[Exact collision quotient for $U$]
-\label{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient}
-For every $m\ge2$,
-\begin{equation}
-\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)
-=\min\{L\ge1:\mathcal N_{U,m,L}=\varnothing\}.
-\label{eq:pisot-exact-depth}
-\end{equation}
-Let $\Gamma_{U,m}$ have vertex set $\Delta_U^{m-1}$ and an edge
-$(v_0,\ldots,v_{m-2})\to(v_1,\ldots,v_{m-2},a)$ exactly when
-\[
-\sum_{j=0}^{m-2}u_jv_j+u_{m-1}a\equiv0\pmod {u_m}.
-\]
-If $B_{U,m}$ is the set of vertices with first coordinate nonzero, then
-\begin{equation}
-\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)=1+\sup\{\text{edge length of a path from }B_{U,m}\}.
-\label{eq:pisot-longest-path}
-\end{equation}
-Moreover, $\Phi_{U,m}$ is injective if and only if no directed cycle of
-$\Gamma_{U,m}$ is reachable from $B_{U,m}$.
-\end{lemma}

-\begin{proof}
-Two folded windows agree exactly when the difference of their raw values is

-equivalent to a vector in $\mathcal N_{U,m,L}$, with no lost collisions.

-\begin{lemma}[Adjacent-window Pisot contraction]
-\label{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction}
-Suppose that $\beta$ is nonintegral, $m\ge m_U$, and two consecutive rows
-of \eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} hold.  Then
-\begin{equation}
-k_{t+1}=0,\qquad e_{t+m}=-k_t.
-\label{eq:pisot-carry-collapse}
-\end{equation}
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-For each embedding define
-\[
-A_{t,i}=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}e_{t+j}\beta_i^j-k_t\beta_i^m.
-\]
-Substitution of \eqref{eq:pisot-binet} into

-$\sum_i c_iA_{t,i}=0$.  For $i\ge1$,
-\[
- |A_{t,i}|\le \frac{d_U}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_U^{*},
-\]

-\begin{corollary}[Global overlap dichotomy for bounded zero representations]
-\label{cor:pisot-zero-strip-synchronization}
-For a fixed strictly increasing Pisot numeration $U$ as in the theorem and an
-aperture $m\ge2$,
-consider all bounded zero words of length $m+1$ of the form
-\[
-[e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0
-\]
-which overlap one digit at a time.  Each row is a standard bounded
-$U$-representation of zero; only its organization into this one-position
-overlap chain is specific here.  Exactly one of the following global
-alternatives holds: some chain with a nonzero coefficient has a finite prefix
-followed by a periodic bounded zero representation; or every nonzero chain
-has fewer than $(C_U+1)m$ rows.  The latter bound has sharp order $\Theta(m)$
-for $U_\theta$.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The overlapping rows are exactly paths in $\Gamma_{U,m}$ by
-\eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}.  A cycle reachable from $B_{U,m}$ gives
-the first alternative by repeating the cycle.  If no such cycle is
-reachable, \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1} bounds every path from $B_{U,m}$.
-Unless a chain is zero, at most $m-1$ initial shifts pass before one of its
-nonzero coordinates occupies the first position, after which fewer than
-$C_Um$ further rows are possible.  The two alternatives are mutually
-exclusive because the periodic tail makes chains arbitrarily long.  The
-words $E_m$ in \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3} give the matching lower order for
-$U_\theta$.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{lemma}[Adjacent collapse for an arbitrary bounded coefficient alphabet]
-\label{lem:bounded-zero-arbitrary-alphabet-collapse}

-the minimal polynomial of a nonintegral Pisot number $\beta$, and fix

-\[

-\]

-For $i\ge1$,
-\[
-|A_{t,i}|\le\frac{D}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_{U,D},

-Direct subtraction of the adjacent dominant-embedding sums gives the exact

-\begin{theorem}[Linear transient bound for bounded $U$-representations of zero]
-\label{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient}
-Let $U=(u_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
-with $u_0=1$, satisfying the integral recurrence whose characteristic
-polynomial is the minimal polynomial of a nonintegral Pisot number $\beta$.
-Fix $D\ge1$.  For $m\ge2$, let $G_m(U,D)$ be the directed graph with vertex
-set
-\[
-([-D,D]\cap\mathbb Z)^{m-1}.
-\]
-There is an edge
-\[
-(e_0,\ldots,e_{m-2})\longrightarrow
-(e_1,\ldots,e_{m-2},e_{m-1})
-\]
-if and only if there is an integer $c$ such that
-\begin{equation}
-e_0u_0+e_1u_1+\cdots+e_{m-1}u_{m-1}+cu_m=0.
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-overlap-edge}
-\end{equation}
-The completing coefficient is unique and necessarily satisfies
-$|c|\le K_{U,D}$.
-Then there is an effectively computable $C(U,D)<\infty$ such that, for every
-$m\ge2$, if no directed cycle of $G_m(U,D)$ is reachable from a vertex whose
-first coordinate is nonzero, every directed path beginning at such a vertex
-has fewer than $C(U,D)m$ edges.
-
-Equivalently, after shifting a chain so that its initial exposed coefficient
-is nonzero, either it reaches a directed cycle, or it has fewer than
-$C(U,D)m$ further overlaps.  The graphs are finite-state recognizers of these
-overlap chains, and their edges are bounded $U$-representations of zero by
-\eqref{eq:bounded-zero-overlap-edge}.
-
-The linear order is sharp.  For the fixed recurrence
-\[
-u_0=1,\quad u_1=2,\quad u_2=4,\qquad
-u_{n+3}=2u_{n+2}-u_{n+1}+u_n,
-\]
-whose leading root is the Pisot root of $x^3-2x^2+x-1$, and for $D=1$, the
-maximum finite path length is at least $m-3$ for every $m\ge4$.
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}

-$|k_t|\le K_{U,D}$ uniformly in $m$.  Suppose first that

-\ref{lem:bounded-zero-arbitrary-alphabet-collapse}, applied to each adjacent

-\[
-k_1=k_2=\cdots=0,\qquad

-\]
-A path of $m+1$ edges therefore reaches the all-zero vertex.  That vertex
-has a loop, so such a path would make a directed cycle reachable from its
-initial vertex.  Under the hypothesis of the theorem, every path has at
-most $m$ edges for $m\ge m_0(U,D)$.
-
-For each of the finitely many $2\le m<m_0(U,D)$, the graph is finite.  When
-no cycle is reachable from the first-coordinate-nonzero vertices, exact
-acyclic longest-path search computes the maximum $p_{U,D}(m)$; set it to
-zero otherwise.  Thus, for example,
-\[
-C(U,D)=\max\left(2,
- \max_{2\le m<m_0(U,D)}
- \left\lceil\frac{1+p_{U,D}(m)}m\right\rceil\right)
-\]
-is effective and has the required property, with the inner maximum understood
-as zero when $m_0(U,D)=2$.
-
-For sharpness, the coefficient words $E_m$ in

-classified in \eqref{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization}--

-paths in $G_m(U,1)$ of length
-$2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-2\ge m-3$.  The next bounded-coefficient path set is
-empty by the same exact terminal calculation, so no reachable cycle occurs.
-This conclusion uses the recurrence identities alone, independently of any
-realization of the coefficients as differences of raw words.
+Finally, the same collision rows are exactly edges of $G_m(U_\theta,1)$.
+The vectors $\pm E_m$ give paths of length $\lambda_m-1$, while the empty
+next obstruction set rules out any longer path or reachable cycle.  Since
+$\lambda_m-1\ge m-3$, this proves the two asserted sharpness conclusions.
 \end{proof}

-\begin{remark}[Logical boundary of the standard-object theorem]
-\label{rem:bounded-zero-standard-object-boundary}
-The statement and proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient}
-use only a fixed Pisot recurrence, bounded integer coefficients, the
-distinguished weight $u_m$, and one-position overlaps of bounded
-$U$-representations of zero.  They use no canonical rank bijection, legal-word
-alphabet, cyclic reduction map, positive/negative realization of
-coefficients, image shift, or inverse decoder.  The distinguished modulus
-$u_m$ and consecutive recurrence weights remain essential: replacing $u_m$
-by an unrelated modulus destroys \eqref{eq:bounded-zero-adjacent-identity}.
-The theorem therefore does not concern numerical $\beta$-normalization,
-successor carry propagation, general synchronized transductions, general
-right-closing maps, or a broad class of sliding block codes.
-\end{remark}

+\section{Comparative context}
+\label{sec:comparative-context}
+
+The fixed cubic theorem and the broader family results answer different
+questions.  Theorem~\ref{thm:fixed-cubic-sharpness} keeps the recurrence,
+alphabet, and base fixed while the aperture grows.  Its limit
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)/m\to1$ proves that a theorem uniform over fixed
+Pisot systems cannot improve the order $O_U(m)$ to $o(m)$.  By contrast,
+Bassino's cubic construction varies the base with the desired inverse
+length \cite{Bassino2002}.  Varying-system unboundedness does not establish a
+lower order inside any one recurrence, while fixed-system sharpness does not
+classify how exact thresholds change across a parameter family.
+
+The base $\theta$ is also a canonical simple-Parry example:
+$d_\theta(1)=1101\,0^\infty$.  That identification supplies the legal
+language and its rank recurrence, but the proof of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:fixed-cubic-sharpness} uses none of the general
+simple-Parry quotient theory.  After the Parry word is checked, the argument
+needs only the recurrence for $Q_j(\theta)$, a direct quotient bound, the
+contracting-conjugate estimate, the suffix-sum identity, and the terminal
+integer equations.  Keeping that proof here makes the sharpness statement
+logically complete rather than treating it as computational evidence.
+
+Quadratic Pisot systems behave more rigidly.  Their least nontrivial cyclic
+rank threshold is always two or three, and their exact future-only inverse
+lengths are bounded by much smaller formulas than the fixed cubic sequence
+above.  Those facts do not enter the contraction theorem: the proof of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient} neither specializes the
+degree nor uses a classification of legal languages.  Conversely, the
+quadratic classification depends on exact chamber arithmetic, critical
+fibers, Fischer covers, and Markov order, which would obscure the
+bounded-zero mechanism if reproduced here.
+
+The companion article by the present authors, \emph{Exact overlap thresholds
+and future-only inverse depth for cyclic ranks of quadratic and simple-Parry
+beta-languages}, develops those comparisons in full.  It contains the
+explicit Fibonacci model, the complete quadratic-Pisot threshold and local
+structure, the coordinate-difference quotient for arbitrary nonintegral
+simple-Parry bases, and Bassino-family unboundedness.  No result from that
+article is used in Sections~\ref{sec:bounded-zero-transients}--
+\ref{sec:fixed-cubic-sharpness}; the only shared material is the definition
+of cyclic language-rank recoding and the distinction from numerical
+$\beta$-normalization.
+
+This separation also fixes the meaning of the sharpness claim.  The
+effective constant $C(U,D)$ includes exact longest-path searches at the
+finitely many apertures below the contraction threshold.  We do not claim
+that this particular constant is optimal.  Sharpness refers to growth order:
+for the single recurrence $U_\theta$ and the fixed coefficient alphabet
+$\{-1,0,1\}$, the exact longest finite path is
+$2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-2$, hence asymptotic to $m$.  The same terminal words
+are realized as raw digit differences, so the corresponding inverse length
+is one larger.  The graph theorem and its cyclic-rank corollary therefore
+have matching linear lower order for the same fixed arithmetic object.

+\section{Scope of the audit}
+
+This document records finite checks supporting implementation and
+reproducibility.  None of the checks replaces a proof in the article.  In
+particular, the arbitrary-alphabet adjacent collapse, the linear transient
+bound, the exact collision quotient, and the fixed cubic terminal
+classification are all proved in the main text.
+
+\section{Small-aperture cubic records}
+
+For the recurrence
+\[
+Q_0=1,\quad Q_1=2,\quad Q_2=4,\qquad
+Q_{j+3}=2Q_{j+2}-Q_{j+1}+Q_j,
+\]
+the first values are
+\[
+1,2,4,7,12,21,37,65,114,200,351.
+\]
+At aperture four the asserted causal length is three.  Exhaustive integer
+division of the two collision rows over $\{-1,0,1\}$ gives
+\[
+\mathcal N_{\theta,4,2}
+=\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1)\},
+\qquad
+\mathcal N_{\theta,4,3}=\varnothing.
+\]
+At aperture five the asserted causal length is three, and the corresponding
+record is
+\[
+\mathcal N_{\theta,5,2}
+=\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1,0)\},
+\qquad
+\mathcal N_{\theta,5,3}=\varnothing.
+\]
+The verification script enumerates the bounded coefficient vectors directly,
+checks divisibility of each consecutive window sum by $Q_m$, and compares
+the resulting sets with these signed terminal words.
+
+For $6\le m\le12$, the script constructs $E_m$ from its recursion and checks
+all of the following exact integer assertions: every coefficient belongs to
+$\{-1,0,1\}$; the first coefficient is nonzero; the first
+$\lambda_m-1$ window sums are multiples of $Q_m$; the signed pair
+$\{E_m,-E_m\}$ exhausts the penultimate obstruction set; and the next
+obstruction set is empty.  The finite range is a regression boundary only.
+The proof for all $m$ is the suffix-sum argument in the main article.
+
+\section{Root-isolation arithmetic}
+
+The cubic $f(x)=x^3-2x^2+x-1$ satisfies
+\[
+f(7/4)=-\frac1{64}<0,
+\qquad
+f(351/200)=\frac{3151}{8000000}>0.
+\]
+Its derivative has critical points $1/3$ and $1$, and $f$ is negative at
+both; hence the interval isolates its only real root $\theta$.  If
+$\rho,\overline\rho$ are the other roots, Vieta's formula gives
+$|\rho|^2=1/\theta$ and therefore $|\rho|<0.756$ on the isolating interval.
+
+The generating function
+\[
+\sum_{n\ge0}Q_nz^n=\frac{1+z^2}{1-2z+z^2-z^3}
+\]
+gives, by residues,
+\[
+c_\alpha=\frac{\alpha^2+1}{3\alpha^2-4\alpha+1}
+\]
+for every root $\alpha$.  Exact rational endpoint substitution, together
+with the conjugate relation, yields
+\[
+1.26<c_\theta<1.27,qquad |c_\rho|<0.19.
+\]
+Consequently the nondominant contribution in either adjacent window is less
+than $1.54$.  The exact finite separation for
+$a,k,l\in\{-1,0,1\}$ is bounded below by
+$2-\theta>0.245$, and endpoint arithmetic gives
+\[
+\theta^6(2-\theta)>7.03
+>1+(1+\theta)1.54.
+\]
+These inequalities audit the claim that adjacent collapse holds from
+aperture six onward.  The small-aperture enumeration above handles four and
+five; no floating-point comparison enters the proof.
+
+\section{Seven-edge anchored regression}
+
+The repaired edge definition allows a body coefficient bound $D$ and a
+separately bounded completing coefficient.  For the nonstandard initial
+values $(u_0,u_1,u_2)=(1,2,4)$, aperture $m=2$, and $D=2$, direct enumeration
+finds exactly the seven triples $(e_0,e_1,c)$ satisfying
+\[
+e_0u_0+e_1u_1+cu_2=0:
+\]
+\[
+(-2,-1,1),\ (-2,1,0),\ (0,-2,1),\ (0,0,0),\
+(0,2,-1),\ (2,-1,0),\ (2,1,-1).
+\]
+The induced nonzero transitions are
+\[
+-2\longrightarrow\{-1,1\},\qquad
+2\longrightarrow\{-1,1\},
+\]
+while $-1$ and $1$ have no outgoing edges.  Thus no directed cycle is
+reachable from a nonzero vertex.  An unanchored formulation would nevertheless
+admit arbitrarily long zero padding before the nonzero transition.  The main
+article avoids that false equivalence by shifting the chain so that its
+initial exposed coefficient is nonzero.  The test reports the literal marker
+\path{unanchored-chain regression edges=7} only after comparing the full
+edge set above.
+
+\section{Arbitrary-alphabet falsification battery}
+
+The second audit uses the Pisot root of
+$x^3-3x^2+2x-1$, which does not satisfy Condition~F.  It checks coefficient
+bounds $D=2,3$ for both the canonical count recurrence and the nonstandard
+initial values $(1,2,4)$.  For each of twelve adjacent-window cases, the
+script enumerates the body coefficients and integer quotients and verifies
+the conclusion
+\[
+k_{t+1}=0,\qquad e_{t+m}=-k_t
+\]
+at and beyond the audited contraction thresholds.  Testing a
+non-Condition-F system guards against accidentally importing zero
+preservation into the implementation.  The proof in the article uses only
+the Pisot embeddings and the finite algebraic separation.
+
+\section{Reproduction and integrity}
+
+From the article directory, run
+\begin{verbatim}
+python artifacts/verify_fixed_cubic_audit.py
+python artifacts/test_bounded_zero_arbitrary_D.py
+\end{verbatim}
+The expected saved outputs are
+\path{artifacts/fixed_cubic_audit_verification.txt} and
+\path{artifacts/bounded_zero_arbitrary_D_verification.txt}.  File hashes are
+listed in \path{artifacts/SHA256SUMS}; paths are relative to the artifacts
+directory and the checksum file uses LF line endings.

+\begin{abstract}
+We study one-position overlap chains of bounded representations of zero in a
+fixed Pisot linear numeration system.  If $U=(u_j)$ is strictly increasing,
+$u_0=1$, and its recurrence has a nonintegral Pisot characteristic root,
+then for every fixed coefficient bound $D$ there is an effective constant
+$C(U,D)$.  Unless a nonzero overlap chain reaches a directed cycle, its
+transient has fewer than $C(U,D)m$ edges at aperture $m$.  The proof uses an
+arbitrary-alphabet adjacent-collapse lemma: contracting conjugates force the
+second quotient in two consecutive zero representations to vanish and fix
+the newly exposed coefficient.  No Condition~F or zero-preservation
+hypothesis is required.
+
+As an exact application, consider the cyclic rank recoding obtained by
+extending the canonical rank of legal length-$m$ words to the full digit
+cube and reducing it modulo $u_m$.  Its coordinatewise-difference graph is
+exactly the bounded-zero overlap graph for the canonical difference
+alphabet.  Hence injectivity implies an aperture-linear future-only inverse
+depth.  A fixed binary cubic recurrence with leading root of
+$x^3-2x^2+x-1$ attains the linear order: for every $m\ge4$ its cyclic rank
+recoding is injective and has exact causal length
+$2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-1$.  We classify the penultimate obstruction set as
+$\{E_m,-E_m\}$ and prove that the next set is empty.  The same words show
+that the bounded-zero transient bound itself has sharp linear order.
+\end{abstract}
+
+\medskip
+\noindent{\bf 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification.}
+Primary: 37B10, 11B39; Secondary: 11A67, 37B40.
+
+\medskip
+\noindent{\bf Key words and phrases.}
+Pisot numeration, bounded representation of zero, overlap graph, linear
+transient, cyclic rank recoding, future-only inverse, collision quotient.

+\section{Introduction}
+\label{sec:introduction}
+
+Bounded representations of zero are a standard finite-state object in
+Pisot numeration.  Their regularity supports normalization and arithmetic
+algorithms, but regularity by itself does not control how long an
+aperture-dependent chain of overlapping zero representations can remain
+transient.  We consider the following narrow quantitative question.  Fix a
+Pisot recurrence $U=(u_j)$ and a coefficient alphabet $[-D,D]\cap\mathbb Z$.
+At aperture $m$, use a length-$m$ coefficient word as a state transition
+exactly when it can be completed by a coefficient of the distinguished
+weight $u_m$ to represent zero.  Consecutive edges overlap by one position.
+How long can a path beginning with an exposed nonzero coefficient survive if
+it never reaches a cycle?
+
+Our first main result, Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient}, gives
+an effective linear answer.  There is a computable $C(U,D)<\infty$ such that
+every such transient has fewer than $C(U,D)m$ edges.  Equivalently, after a
+nonzero chain is anchored at its first exposed nonzero coefficient, it
+either enters a repeatable periodic tail or has only linearly many further
+overlaps.  The coefficient completing an edge is not assumed to belong to
+$[-D,D]$; it is proved to lie in a fixed interval
+$[-K_{U,D},K_{U,D}]$.  This mixed-alphabet point is essential to the correct
+edge formulation.
+
+The mechanism is local.  Lemma
+\ref{lem:bounded-zero-arbitrary-alphabet-collapse} compares two consecutive
+zero representations under every algebraic embedding.  The contracting
+conjugates bound the nondominant sums, while a finite exact separation in the
+dominant embedding prevents any nonzero value of
+$e_{t+m}+k_t-\beta k_{t+1}$ once $m$ is large enough.  Irrationality then
+forces
+\[
+k_{t+1}=0,\qquad e_{t+m}=-k_t.
+\]
+Along a path, every quotient after the first vanishes and all later appended
+coefficients vanish after one exceptional position.  A path of $m+1$ edges
+therefore reaches the zero state, which already has a loop.  The finitely
+many smaller apertures are handled by exact acyclic longest-path searches.
+This gives an effective constant without counting all
+$(2D+1)^{m-1}$ states.
+
+The proof requires neither Condition~F nor preservation of leading zeros.
+Finite-state recognition of bounded zero representations in Pisot systems is
+classical \cite{Frougny1992}, and recent work places zero preservation in a
+precise Condition~F framework \cite{CartonSudberyYassawi2026}.  Those results
+do not imply an aperture-linear survival bound for the moving overlap graphs
+considered here.  Conversely, our result does not assert finite expansion,
+normalization complexity, or a general synchronization theorem.  The
+distinguished terminal weight $u_m$ and consecutive recurrence weights are
+part of the statement.
+
+The second part applies the standard-object theorem to a symbolic recoding.
+For a strictly increasing Pisot numeration system, order the legal
+length-$m$ words by canonical rank, extend the same positional rank to the
+full digit cube, reduce it modulo the number $u_m$ of legal words, and return
+the legal word with that residue.  Overlap these recoded windows along the
+shift.  We call the resulting factor code a cyclic language-rank recoding.
+It is a congruence of integer language ranks, not numerical
+$\beta$-normalization in $\mathbb Z[\beta]$.
+
+Lemma~\ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient} proves that the
+coordinatewise-difference quotient of the pair graph loses no collision:
+every bounded digit difference is realized by its positive and negative
+parts.  The quotient is exactly the graph $G_m(U,d_U)$ from the first part.
+The longest path from a first-coordinate-nonzero state is exactly one less
+than the least future-only inverse window, and injectivity is equivalent to
+the absence of a reachable cycle.  Corollary
+\ref{cor:pisot-linear-causal-depth} therefore gives
+\[
+\Phi_{U,m}\text{ injective}
+\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)\le C_Um. \tag{A1}
+\]
+This is a consequence of the bounded-zero theorem and the exact quotient,
+not the definitional center of the argument.
+
+Classical pair and fiber graphs supply reachable-cycle tests and finite
+inverse windows for injective local maps
+\cite{AmorosoPatt1972,Richardson1972,Nasu1977,Head1989,LindMarcus1995,
+Nasu1995}.  Their generic state-count bound is exponential in $m$ here.
+Likewise, Ashley's decoder-window estimates are linear in the number of
+states of a presenting graph, not in this aperture
+\cite{Ashley1988,Ashley1996}.  The bounded-delay theorem of
+Frougny and Sakarovitch starts from a rational relation already known to have
+bounded delay; it does not derive an $O(m)$ delay from injectivity
+\cite{FrougnySakarovitch1991}.  The arithmetic adjacent-collapse lemma is
+what changes the scale from exponential to linear.
+
+Finally, Theorem~\ref{thm:fixed-cubic-sharpness} proves sharpness inside one
+fixed system.  Let $\theta$ be the leading root of
+$x^3-2x^2+x-1$ and use the binary recurrence beginning $1,2,4$.  For every
+$m\ge4$,
+\[
+\Phi_{\theta,m}\text{ is injective},\qquad
+\ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)=2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-1. \tag{A2}
+\]
+The proof classifies the penultimate obstruction set exactly as
+$\{E_m,-E_m\}$ and the next obstruction set as empty.  Read only as bounded
+coefficient words, the same $E_m$ give paths of length at least $m-3$ in
+$G_m(U_\theta,1)$.  One object therefore proves sharpness both for the
+inverse-depth corollary and for the bounded-zero transient theorem.
+
+The article is organized in this logical order.  Section
+\ref{sec:bounded-zero-transients} defines the overlap chains, proves the
+arbitrary-alphabet collapse lemma, and proves the linear transient theorem.
+Section~\ref{sec:cyclic-rank-application} introduces cyclic ranks, proves the
+exact collision quotient, and deduces \textup{(A1)}.  Section
+\ref{sec:fixed-cubic-sharpness} proves \textup{(A2)}--\textup{(A3)} and the
+terminal classification.  Section~\ref{sec:comparative-context} records the
+limited comparison with the family-classification problem.  The companion
+article by the present authors, \emph{Exact overlap thresholds and
+future-only inverse depth for cyclic ranks of quadratic and simple-Parry
+beta-languages}, contains the full Fibonacci, quadratic, and simple-Parry
+classification.

-If each output word is relabeled by its canonical rank in
-$\mathbb Z/u_m\mathbb Z$, the local rule is
-\[
-(x_0,\ldots,x_{m-1})\longmapsto
-\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_jx_j\pmod {u_m}.
-\]
-Thus the word-valued rule is a symbolwise bijective relabeling of a modular
-weighted sliding block code.  The weights, the modulus $u_m$, and their
-variation with $m$ are specific to the present family.  This is not a linear
-cellular automaton: in general $D_U$ is only a digit subset of
-$\mathbb Z/u_m\mathbb Z$, not a module on which the rule is a group
-endomorphism.
-
-The scope is not a disguised standard-initial-value convention.  For
-example, standard $k$-bonacci initial conditions begin $1,1,\ldots$ and fail
-strict increase, whereas the customary shift beginning $1,2,\ldots$ belongs
-to the present class.  Nor do we assume Condition~F: that would be a genuine
-restriction, since the principal root of $x^3-3x^2+2x-1$ is Pisot but does
-not satisfy Condition~F \cite[Theorem~3]{Akiyama2000}.  The equivalence of
-Condition~F with zero preservation is proved in
-\cite{CartonSudberyYassawi2026}, but neither property is used below.

-\begin{lemma}[Exact collision quotient for $U$]

-For every $m\ge2$,

-Let $\Gamma_{U,m}$ have vertex set $\Delta_U^{m-1}$ and an edge

-\begin{proof}
-Two folded windows agree exactly when the difference of their raw values is
-divisible by $u_m$, because the canonical normal words represent
-$0,\ldots,u_m-1$ bijectively.  Every $e\in\Delta_U$ is realized as a
-difference of two digits by taking its positive and negative parts in

-equivalent to a vector in $\mathcal N_{U,m,L}$, with no lost collisions.
-Reading consecutive difference windows gives precisely the paths from
-$B_{U,m}$ in $\Gamma_{U,m}$, proving \eqref{eq:pisot-exact-depth} and
-\eqref{eq:pisot-longest-path}.  A reachable nonzero cycle can be repeated
-periodically and is realized by two raw points.

-\begin{theorem}[Fixed-base linear causal depth and sharpness for Pisot numeration]
-\label{thm:pisot-linear-depth-sharpness}

-\end{equation*}

-\begin{corollary}[Global overlap dichotomy for bounded zero representations]
-\label{cor:pisot-zero-strip-synchronization}
-For a fixed strictly increasing Pisot numeration $U$ as in the theorem and an
-aperture $m\ge2$,

-alternatives holds: some chain with a nonzero coefficient has a finite prefix
-followed by a periodic bounded zero representation; or every nonzero chain

-exclusive because the periodic tail makes chains arbitrarily long.  The

-$U_\theta$.
-\end{proof}

+The theorem also gives the useful global chain dichotomy.  Consider all
+bounded zero words of length $m+1$ that overlap one digit at a time.  Either
+some chain with a nonzero coefficient has a finite prefix followed by a
+periodic bounded zero representation, or every nonzero chain has fewer than
+$(C(U,D)+1)m$ rows.  Indeed, a reachable cycle gives the periodic tail.  In
+the absence of such a cycle, at most $m-1$ initial shifts pass before a
+nonzero coordinate occupies the first position, after which the theorem
+bounds the remaining overlaps.  The alternatives are mutually exclusive
+because a periodic tail can be repeated to make arbitrarily long chains.

-For $m=4,5$, successive exact division in the two or three window
-congruences gives
-\[
-\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
-m&Q_m&\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m-1}
-&\mathcal N_{\theta,m,\lambda_m}\\ \hline
-4&12&\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1)\}&\varnothing\\
-5&21&\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1,0)\}&\varnothing.
-\end{array}
-\]
-This is an exhaustive integer calculation: in each row the quotient is in
-$\{-1,0,1\}$ by \eqref{eq:theta-carry-one}, and the last digit determines
-the preceding bounded digit successively.  Thus \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3}
-holds for every $m\ge4$.  Lemma
-\ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient} now gives
-\eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A2}, including injectivity, and the limiting statement
-is immediate.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Global overlap dichotomy for bounded zero representations]
-\label{cor:pisot-zero-strip-synchronization}
-For a fixed strictly increasing Pisot numeration $U$ as in the theorem and an
-aperture $m\ge2$,
-consider all bounded zero words of length $m+1$ of the form
-\[
-[e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0
-\]
-which overlap one digit at a time.  Each row is a standard bounded
-$U$-representation of zero; only its organization into this one-position
-overlap chain is specific here.  Exactly one of the following global
-alternatives holds: some chain with a nonzero coefficient has a finite prefix
-followed by a periodic bounded zero representation; or every nonzero chain
-has fewer than $(C_U+1)m$ rows.  The latter bound has sharp order $\Theta(m)$
-for $U_\theta$.
 \end{corollary}
 
 \begin{proof}
-The overlapping rows are exactly paths in $\Gamma_{U,m}$ by
-\eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}.  A cycle reachable from $B_{U,m}$ gives
-the first alternative by repeating the cycle.  If no such cycle is
-reachable, \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1} bounds every path from $B_{U,m}$.
-Unless a chain is zero, at most $m-1$ initial shifts pass before one of its
-nonzero coordinates occupies the first position, after which fewer than
-$C_Um$ further rows are possible.  The two alternatives are mutually
-exclusive because the periodic tail makes chains arbitrarily long.  The
-words $E_m$ in \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3} give the matching lower order for
-$U_\theta$.
-\end{proof}
-
-We now detach the contraction argument from the canonical digit-difference
-alphabet.  Fix $D\ge1$ and retain the effective Binet and growth data in
-\eqref{eq:pisot-binet}--\eqref{eq:pisot-effective-growth}.  Put
-\begin{equation}
-K_{U,D}=\left\lceil\frac{DA_U}{b_U(\beta-1)}\right\rceil
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-carry-bound}
-\end{equation}
-and
-\begin{equation}
-\delta_{U,D}=\min\left\{|a+k-\beta l|:
- |a|\le D,\ |k|,|l|\le K_{U,D},\ a+k-\beta l\ne0\right\}.
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-separation}
-\end{equation}
-The variables in this minimum are integers.  Since $\beta$ is irrational,
-$\delta_{U,D}>0$, and exact algebraic-number comparison computes it.  Define
-\begin{align}
-M_{U,D}&=\frac1{c_0}\sum_{i=1}^{s-1}|c_i|
- \left(\frac{D}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_{U,D}\right),\nonumber\\
-B_{U,D}&=D+(1+\beta)M_{U,D},
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-conjugate-bound}
-\end{align}
-and
-\begin{equation}
-m_0(U,D)=\min\{m\ge2:\beta^m\delta_{U,D}>B_{U,D}\}.
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-contraction-threshold}
-\end{equation}
-All these constants are effective from $U$ and $D$.

-\begin{lemma}[Adjacent collapse for an arbitrary bounded coefficient alphabet]
-\label{lem:bounded-zero-arbitrary-alphabet-collapse}
-Let $U$ satisfy the integral recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is
-the minimal polynomial of a nonintegral Pisot number $\beta$, and fix
-$D\ge1$.  If $m\ge m_0(U,D)$, coefficients
-$e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m}\in[-D,D]\cap\mathbb Z$, and integers $k_t,k_{t+1}$
-satisfy
-\[
-\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_je_{t+j}=k_tu_m,
-\qquad
-\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_je_{t+1+j}=k_{t+1}u_m,
-\]
-then
-\[
-k_{t+1}=0,\qquad e_{t+m}=-k_t.
-\]
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The growth bounds give, for either row,
-\[
-|k_t|\le D\frac{\sum_{j<m}u_j}{u_m}
- <\frac{DA_U}{b_U(\beta-1)}\le K_{U,D},
-\]
-and similarly $|k_{t+1}|\le K_{U,D}$.  For every embedding set
-\[
-A_{t,i}=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}e_{t+j}\beta_i^j-k_t\beta_i^m.
-\]
-The recurrence and its Binet expansion give $\sum_i c_iA_{t,i}=0$.
-For $i\ge1$,
-\[
-|A_{t,i}|\le\frac{D}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_{U,D},
-\]
-so $|A_{t,0}|\le M_{U,D}$, and the same holds at $t+1$.
-Direct subtraction of the adjacent dominant-embedding sums gives the exact
-identity
-\begin{equation}
-\beta^m(e_{t+m}+k_t-\beta k_{t+1})
-=\beta A_{t+1,0}-A_{t,0}+e_t.
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-adjacent-identity}
-\end{equation}
-The right side has modulus at most $B_{U,D}$.  If the parenthesis on the
-left were nonzero, \eqref{eq:bounded-zero-separation} and
-\eqref{eq:bounded-zero-contraction-threshold} would make the left side
-strictly larger than $B_{U,D}$, a contradiction.  Hence
-$e_{t+m}+k_t=\beta k_{t+1}$.  Irrationality of $\beta$ and integrality of
-the three coefficients force $k_{t+1}=0$ and $e_{t+m}=-k_t$.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Linear transient bound for bounded $U$-representations of zero]
-\label{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient}
-Let $U=(u_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
-with $u_0=1$, satisfying the integral recurrence whose characteristic
-polynomial is the minimal polynomial of a nonintegral Pisot number $\beta$.
-Fix $D\ge1$.  For $m\ge2$, let $G_m(U,D)$ be the directed graph with vertex
-set
-\[
-([-D,D]\cap\mathbb Z)^{m-1}.
-\]
-There is an edge
-\[
-(e_0,\ldots,e_{m-2})\longrightarrow
-(e_1,\ldots,e_{m-2},e_{m-1})
-\]
-if and only if there is an integer $c$ such that
-\begin{equation}
-e_0u_0+e_1u_1+\cdots+e_{m-1}u_{m-1}+cu_m=0.
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-overlap-edge}
-\end{equation}
-The completing coefficient is unique and necessarily satisfies
-$|c|\le K_{U,D}$.
-Then there is an effectively computable $C(U,D)<\infty$ such that, for every
-$m\ge2$, if no directed cycle of $G_m(U,D)$ is reachable from a vertex whose
-first coordinate is nonzero, every directed path beginning at such a vertex
-has fewer than $C(U,D)m$ edges.
-
-Equivalently, after shifting a chain so that its initial exposed coefficient
-is nonzero, either it reaches a directed cycle, or it has fewer than
-$C(U,D)m$ further overlaps.  The graphs are finite-state recognizers of these
-overlap chains, and their edges are bounded $U$-representations of zero by
-\eqref{eq:bounded-zero-overlap-edge}.
-
-The linear order is sharp.  For the fixed recurrence
-\[
-u_0=1,\quad u_1=2,\quad u_2=4,\qquad
-u_{n+3}=2u_{n+2}-u_{n+1}+u_n,
-\]
-whose leading root is the Pisot root of $x^3-2x^2+x-1$, and for $D=1$, the
-maximum finite path length is at least $m-3$ for every $m\ge4$.
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-For an edge at time $t$, write $k_t=-c$ in
-\eqref{eq:bounded-zero-overlap-edge}.  The growth estimate gives
-$|k_t|\le K_{U,D}$ uniformly in $m$.  Suppose first that
-$m\ge m_0(U,D)$.  Along any path of at least two edges, Lemma
-\ref{lem:bounded-zero-arbitrary-alphabet-collapse}, applied to each adjacent
-pair, gives
-\[
-k_1=k_2=\cdots=0,\qquad
-e_m=-k_0,\qquad e_{m+1}=e_{m+2}=\cdots=0.
-\]
-A path of $m+1$ edges therefore reaches the all-zero vertex.  That vertex
-has a loop, so such a path would make a directed cycle reachable from its
-initial vertex.  Under the hypothesis of the theorem, every path has at
-most $m$ edges for $m\ge m_0(U,D)$.
-
-For each of the finitely many $2\le m<m_0(U,D)$, the graph is finite.  When
-no cycle is reachable from the first-coordinate-nonzero vertices, exact
-acyclic longest-path search computes the maximum $p_{U,D}(m)$; set it to
-zero otherwise.  Thus, for example,
-\[
-C(U,D)=\max\left(2,
- \max_{2\le m<m_0(U,D)}
- \left\lceil\frac{1+p_{U,D}(m)}m\right\rceil\right)
-\]
-is effective and has the required property, with the inner maximum understood
-as zero when $m_0(U,D)=2$.
-
-For sharpness, the coefficient words $E_m$ in
-\eqref{eq:theta-terminal-word} satisfy the integer recurrence relations
-classified in \eqref{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization}--
-\eqref{eq:theta-five-tail-table}.  Read only as coefficient words, they give
-paths in $G_m(U,1)$ of length
-$2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-2\ge m-3$.  The next bounded-coefficient path set is
-empty by the same exact terminal calculation, so no reachable cycle occurs.
-This conclusion uses the recurrence identities alone, independently of any
-realization of the coefficients as differences of raw words.
+If the Pisot root has degree one, then $u_j=b^j$,
+$D_U=\{0,\ldots,b-1\}$, the fold is the identity, and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)=1$; take $C_U=1$.  Otherwise apply
+Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient} with $D=d_U$.  Its graph is
+exactly $\Gamma_{U,m}$, because \eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge} is the
+edge condition \eqref{eq:bounded-zero-overlap-edge-theorem}.  By Lemma
+\ref{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient}, injectivity is equivalent to the
+absence of a reachable cycle and the causal length is one plus the longest
+path length.  Since the theorem gives fewer than $C(U,d_U)m$ edges, the
+integer path length is at most $C(U,d_U)m-1$.  Taking
+$C_U=C(U,d_U)$ proves both formulations.
 \end{proof}
 
-\begin{remark}[Logical boundary of the standard-object theorem]
-\label{rem:bounded-zero-standard-object-boundary}
-The statement and proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient}
-use only a fixed Pisot recurrence, bounded integer coefficients, the
-distinguished weight $u_m$, and one-position overlaps of bounded
-$U$-representations of zero.  They use no canonical rank bijection, legal-word
-alphabet, cyclic reduction map, positive/negative realization of
-coefficients, image shift, or inverse decoder.  The distinguished modulus
-$u_m$ and consecutive recurrence weights remain essential: replacing $u_m$
-by an unrelated modulus destroys \eqref{eq:bounded-zero-adjacent-identity}.
-The theorem therefore does not concern numerical $\beta$-normalization,
-successor carry propagation, general synchronized transductions, general
-right-closing maps, or a broad class of sliding block codes.
-\end{remark}
+The scope is not a disguised standard-initial-value convention.  For
+example, standard $k$-bonacci initial conditions begin $1,1,\ldots$ and fail
+strict increase, whereas the customary shift beginning $1,2,\ldots$ belongs
+to the present class.  Nor is Condition~F assumed: the principal root of
+$x^3-3x^2+2x-1$ is Pisot but does not satisfy Condition~F
+\cite[Theorem~3]{Akiyama2000}.  The equivalence of Condition~F with zero
+preservation is proved in \cite{CartonSudberyYassawi2026}, but neither
+property enters the corollary.

-\begin{lemma}[Exact collision quotient for $U$]
-\label{lem:pisot-exact-collision-quotient}
-For every $m\ge2$,
-\begin{equation}
-\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)
-=\min\{L\ge1:\mathcal N_{U,m,L}=\varnothing\}.
-\label{eq:pisot-exact-depth}
-\end{equation}
-Let $\Gamma_{U,m}$ have vertex set $\Delta_U^{m-1}$ and an edge
-$(v_0,\ldots,v_{m-2})\to(v_1,\ldots,v_{m-2},a)$ exactly when
-\[

-\]
-If $B_{U,m}$ is the set of vertices with first coordinate nonzero, then
-\begin{equation}
-\ell_{\rm cau}(U,m)=1+\sup\{\text{edge length of a path from }B_{U,m}\}.
-\label{eq:pisot-longest-path}
-\end{equation}
-Moreover, $\Phi_{U,m}$ is injective if and only if no directed cycle of
-$\Gamma_{U,m}$ is reachable from $B_{U,m}$.

-\begin{proof}
-Two folded windows agree exactly when the difference of their raw values is

-\begin{lemma}[Adjacent-window Pisot contraction]
-\label{lem:pisot-adjacent-window-contraction}
-Suppose that $\beta$ is nonintegral, $m\ge m_U$, and two consecutive rows
-of \eqref{eq:pisot-window-carry} hold.  Then
-\begin{equation}

-\begin{proof}
-For each embedding define

-\begin{corollary}[Global overlap dichotomy for bounded zero representations]
-\label{cor:pisot-zero-strip-synchronization}
-For a fixed strictly increasing Pisot numeration $U$ as in the theorem and an
-aperture $m\ge2$,
-consider all bounded zero words of length $m+1$ of the form
-\[
-[e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m-1},-k_t]_U=0
-\]
-which overlap one digit at a time.  Each row is a standard bounded
-$U$-representation of zero; only its organization into this one-position
-overlap chain is specific here.  Exactly one of the following global
-alternatives holds: some chain with a nonzero coefficient has a finite prefix
-followed by a periodic bounded zero representation; or every nonzero chain
-has fewer than $(C_U+1)m$ rows.  The latter bound has sharp order $\Theta(m)$
-for $U_\theta$.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The overlapping rows are exactly paths in $\Gamma_{U,m}$ by
-\eqref{eq:pisot-zero-word-bridge}.  A cycle reachable from $B_{U,m}$ gives
-the first alternative by repeating the cycle.  If no such cycle is
-reachable, \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A1} bounds every path from $B_{U,m}$.
-Unless a chain is zero, at most $m-1$ initial shifts pass before one of its
-nonzero coordinates occupies the first position, after which fewer than
-$C_Um$ further rows are possible.  The two alternatives are mutually
-exclusive because the periodic tail makes chains arbitrarily long.  The
-words $E_m$ in \eqref{eq:pisot-linear-A3} give the matching lower order for
-$U_\theta$.
-\end{proof}

-\label{eq:bounded-zero-carry-bound}

-\end{equation}

-\begin{lemma}[Adjacent collapse for an arbitrary bounded coefficient alphabet]
-\label{lem:bounded-zero-arbitrary-alphabet-collapse}
-Let $U$ satisfy the integral recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is
-the minimal polynomial of a nonintegral Pisot number $\beta$, and fix

-$e_t,\ldots,e_{t+m}\in[-D,D]\cap\mathbb Z$, and integers $k_t,k_{t+1}$
-satisfy
-\[
-\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_je_{t+j}=k_tu_m,

-\[

-The growth bounds give, for either row,
-\[

-\]
-and similarly $|k_{t+1}|\le K_{U,D}$.  For every embedding set
-\[

-\]
-The recurrence and its Binet expansion give $\sum_i c_iA_{t,i}=0$.
-For $i\ge1$,
-\[
-|A_{t,i}|\le\frac{D}{1-|\beta_i|}+K_{U,D},
-\]

-Direct subtraction of the adjacent dominant-embedding sums gives the exact

-the three coefficients force $k_{t+1}=0$ and $e_{t+m}=-k_t$.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Linear transient bound for bounded $U$-representations of zero]
-\label{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient}
-Let $U=(u_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
-with $u_0=1$, satisfying the integral recurrence whose characteristic
-polynomial is the minimal polynomial of a nonintegral Pisot number $\beta$.
-Fix $D\ge1$.  For $m\ge2$, let $G_m(U,D)$ be the directed graph with vertex
-set
-\[
-([-D,D]\cap\mathbb Z)^{m-1}.
-\]
-There is an edge
-\[
-(e_0,\ldots,e_{m-2})\longrightarrow
-(e_1,\ldots,e_{m-2},e_{m-1})
-\]
-if and only if there is an integer $c$ such that
-\begin{equation}
-e_0u_0+e_1u_1+\cdots+e_{m-1}u_{m-1}+cu_m=0.
-\label{eq:bounded-zero-overlap-edge}
-\end{equation}
-The completing coefficient is unique and necessarily satisfies
-$|c|\le K_{U,D}$.
-Then there is an effectively computable $C(U,D)<\infty$ such that, for every
-$m\ge2$, if no directed cycle of $G_m(U,D)$ is reachable from a vertex whose
-first coordinate is nonzero, every directed path beginning at such a vertex
-has fewer than $C(U,D)m$ edges.
-
-Equivalently, after shifting a chain so that its initial exposed coefficient
-is nonzero, either it reaches a directed cycle, or it has fewer than
-$C(U,D)m$ further overlaps.  The graphs are finite-state recognizers of these
-overlap chains, and their edges are bounded $U$-representations of zero by
-\eqref{eq:bounded-zero-overlap-edge}.
-
-The linear order is sharp.  For the fixed recurrence
-\[
-u_0=1,\quad u_1=2,\quad u_2=4,\qquad
-u_{n+3}=2u_{n+2}-u_{n+1}+u_n,
-\]
-whose leading root is the Pisot root of $x^3-2x^2+x-1$, and for $D=1$, the
-maximum finite path length is at least $m-3$ for every $m\ge4$.
-\end{theorem}

-\begin{proof}

-$|k_t|\le K_{U,D}$ uniformly in $m$.  Suppose first that

-\ref{lem:bounded-zero-arbitrary-alphabet-collapse}, applied to each adjacent

-\]
-A path of $m+1$ edges therefore reaches the all-zero vertex.  That vertex
-has a loop, so such a path would make a directed cycle reachable from its
-initial vertex.  Under the hypothesis of the theorem, every path has at
-most $m$ edges for $m\ge m_0(U,D)$.
-
-For each of the finitely many $2\le m<m_0(U,D)$, the graph is finite.  When
-no cycle is reachable from the first-coordinate-nonzero vertices, exact
-acyclic longest-path search computes the maximum $p_{U,D}(m)$; set it to
-zero otherwise.  Thus, for example,
-\[
-C(U,D)=\max\left(2,
- \max_{2\le m<m_0(U,D)}
- \left\lceil\frac{1+p_{U,D}(m)}m\right\rceil\right)
-\]
-is effective and has the required property, with the inner maximum understood
-as zero when $m_0(U,D)=2$.
-
-For sharpness, the coefficient words $E_m$ in

-classified in \eqref{eq:theta-suffix-renormalization}--

-paths in $G_m(U,1)$ of length
-$2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-2\ge m-3$.  The next bounded-coefficient path set is
-empty by the same exact terminal calculation, so no reachable cycle occurs.
-This conclusion uses the recurrence identities alone, independently of any
-realization of the coefficients as differences of raw words.
+Finally, the same collision rows are exactly edges of $G_m(U_\theta,1)$.
+The vectors $\pm E_m$ give paths of length $\lambda_m-1$, while the empty
+next obstruction set rules out any longer path or reachable cycle.  Since
+$\lambda_m-1\ge m-3$, this proves the two asserted sharpness conclusions.
 \end{proof}

-\begin{remark}[Logical boundary of the standard-object theorem]
-\label{rem:bounded-zero-standard-object-boundary}
-The statement and proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient}
-use only a fixed Pisot recurrence, bounded integer coefficients, the
-distinguished weight $u_m$, and one-position overlaps of bounded
-$U$-representations of zero.  They use no canonical rank bijection, legal-word
-alphabet, cyclic reduction map, positive/negative realization of
-coefficients, image shift, or inverse decoder.  The distinguished modulus
-$u_m$ and consecutive recurrence weights remain essential: replacing $u_m$
-by an unrelated modulus destroys \eqref{eq:bounded-zero-adjacent-identity}.
-The theorem therefore does not concern numerical $\beta$-normalization,
-successor carry propagation, general synchronized transductions, general
-right-closing maps, or a broad class of sliding block codes.
-\end{remark}

+\section{Comparative context}
+\label{sec:comparative-context}
+
+The fixed cubic theorem and the broader family results answer different
+questions.  Theorem~\ref{thm:fixed-cubic-sharpness} keeps the recurrence,
+alphabet, and base fixed while the aperture grows.  Its limit
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\theta,m)/m\to1$ proves that a theorem uniform over fixed
+Pisot systems cannot improve the order $O_U(m)$ to $o(m)$.  By contrast,
+Bassino's cubic construction varies the base with the desired inverse
+length \cite{Bassino2002}.  Varying-system unboundedness does not establish a
+lower order inside any one recurrence, while fixed-system sharpness does not
+classify how exact thresholds change across a parameter family.
+
+The base $\theta$ is also a canonical simple-Parry example:
+$d_\theta(1)=1101\,0^\infty$.  That identification supplies the legal
+language and its rank recurrence, but the proof of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:fixed-cubic-sharpness} uses none of the general
+simple-Parry quotient theory.  After the Parry word is checked, the argument
+needs only the recurrence for $Q_j(\theta)$, a direct quotient bound, the
+contracting-conjugate estimate, the suffix-sum identity, and the terminal
+integer equations.  Keeping that proof here makes the sharpness statement
+logically complete rather than treating it as computational evidence.
+
+Quadratic Pisot systems behave more rigidly.  Their least nontrivial cyclic
+rank threshold is always two or three, and their exact future-only inverse
+lengths are bounded by much smaller formulas than the fixed cubic sequence
+above.  Those facts do not enter the contraction theorem: the proof of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-zero-linear-transient} neither specializes the
+degree nor uses a classification of legal languages.  Conversely, the
+quadratic classification depends on exact chamber arithmetic, critical
+fibers, Fischer covers, and Markov order, which would obscure the
+bounded-zero mechanism if reproduced here.
+
+The companion article by the present authors, \emph{Exact overlap thresholds
+and future-only inverse depth for cyclic ranks of quadratic and simple-Parry
+beta-languages}, develops those comparisons in full.  It contains the
+explicit Fibonacci model, the complete quadratic-Pisot threshold and local
+structure, the coordinate-difference quotient for arbitrary nonintegral
+simple-Parry bases, and Bassino-family unboundedness.  No result from that
+article is used in Sections~\ref{sec:bounded-zero-transients}--
+\ref{sec:fixed-cubic-sharpness}; the only shared material is the definition
+of cyclic language-rank recoding and the distinction from numerical
+$\beta$-normalization.
+
+This separation also fixes the meaning of the sharpness claim.  The
+effective constant $C(U,D)$ includes exact longest-path searches at the
+finitely many apertures below the contraction threshold.  We do not claim
+that this particular constant is optimal.  Sharpness refers to growth order:
+for the single recurrence $U_\theta$ and the fixed coefficient alphabet
+$\{-1,0,1\}$, the exact longest finite path is
+$2\lfloor m/2\rfloor-2$, hence asymptotic to $m$.  The same terminal words
+are realized as raw digit differences, so the corresponding inverse length
+is one larger.  The graph theorem and its cyclic-rank corollary therefore
+have matching linear lower order for the same fixed arithmetic object.

+\section*{Data and code availability}
+
+No external data sets were used.  The proofs are analytic.  The accompanying
+source archive contains exact finite computations used as regression and
+falsification checks, not as substitutes for the parameter-uniform proofs.
+The script \path{artifacts/verify_fixed_cubic_audit.py} checks the two small
+apertures, the recursive terminal words, and the exact next-obstruction
+emptiness over the audited range.  The script
+\path{artifacts/test_bounded_zero_arbitrary_D.py} includes the seven-edge
+regression for the anchored edge formulation and exhausts arbitrary-$D$
+adjacent-window cases for a non-Condition-F cubic recurrence.  Saved outputs,
+reproduction commands, and checksums are included under \path{artifacts/}.

+\section{Scope of the audit}
+
+This document records finite checks supporting implementation and
+reproducibility.  None of the checks replaces a proof in the article.  In
+particular, the arbitrary-alphabet adjacent collapse, the linear transient
+bound, the exact collision quotient, and the fixed cubic terminal
+classification are all proved in the main text.
+
+\section{Small-aperture cubic records}
+
+For the recurrence
+\[
+Q_0=1,\quad Q_1=2,\quad Q_2=4,\qquad
+Q_{j+3}=2Q_{j+2}-Q_{j+1}+Q_j,
+\]
+the first values are
+\[
+1,2,4,7,12,21,37,65,114,200,351.
+\]
+At aperture four the asserted causal length is three.  Exhaustive integer
+division of the two collision rows over $\{-1,0,1\}$ gives
+\[
+\mathcal N_{\theta,4,2}
+=\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1)\},
+\qquad
+\mathcal N_{\theta,4,3}=\varnothing.
+\]
+At aperture five the asserted causal length is three, and the corresponding
+record is
+\[
+\mathcal N_{\theta,5,2}
+=\{\pm(1,-1,-1,-1,1,0)\},
+\qquad
+\mathcal N_{\theta,5,3}=\varnothing.
+\]
+The verification script enumerates the bounded coefficient vectors directly,
+checks divisibility of each consecutive window sum by $Q_m$, and compares
+the resulting sets with these signed terminal words.
+
+For $6\le m\le12$, the script constructs $E_m$ from its recursion and checks
+all of the following exact integer assertions: every coefficient belongs to
+$\{-1,0,1\}$; the first coefficient is nonzero; the first
+$\lambda_m-1$ window sums are multiples of $Q_m$; the signed pair
+$\{E_m,-E_m\}$ exhausts the penultimate obstruction set; and the next
+obstruction set is empty.  The finite range is a regression boundary only.
+The proof for all $m$ is the suffix-sum argument in the main article.
+
+\section{Root-isolation arithmetic}
+
+The cubic $f(x)=x^3-2x^2+x-1$ satisfies
+\[
+f(7/4)=-\frac1{64}<0,
+\qquad
+f(351/200)=\frac{3151}{8000000}>0.
+\]
+Its derivative has critical points $1/3$ and $1$, and $f$ is negative at
+both; hence the interval isolates its only real root $\theta$.  If
+$\rho,\overline\rho$ are the other roots, Vieta's formula gives
+$|\rho|^2=1/\theta$ and therefore $|\rho|<0.756$ on the isolating interval.
+
+The generating function
+\[
+\sum_{n\ge0}Q_nz^n=\frac{1+z^2}{1-2z+z^2-z^3}
+\]
+gives, by residues,
+\[
+c_\alpha=\frac{\alpha^2+1}{3\alpha^2-4\alpha+1}
+\]
+for every root $\alpha$.  Exact rational endpoint substitution, together
+with the conjugate relation, yields
+\[
+1.26<c_\theta<1.27,qquad |c_\rho|<0.19.
+\]
+Consequently the nondominant contribution in either adjacent window is less
+than $1.54$.  The exact finite separation for
+$a,k,l\in\{-1,0,1\}$ is bounded below by
+$2-\theta>0.245$, and endpoint arithmetic gives
+\[
+\theta^6(2-\theta)>7.03
+>1+(1+\theta)1.54.
+\]
+These inequalities audit the claim that adjacent collapse holds from
+aperture six onward.  The small-aperture enumeration above handles four and
+five; no floating-point comparison enters the proof.
+
+\section{Seven-edge anchored regression}
+
+The repaired edge definition allows a body coefficient bound $D$ and a
+separately bounded completing coefficient.  For the nonstandard initial
+values $(u_0,u_1,u_2)=(1,2,4)$, aperture $m=2$, and $D=2$, direct enumeration
+finds exactly the seven triples $(e_0,e_1,c)$ satisfying
+\[
+e_0u_0+e_1u_1+cu_2=0:
+\]
+\[
+(-2,-1,1),\ (-2,1,0),\ (0,-2,1),\ (0,0,0),\
+(0,2,-1),\ (2,-1,0),\ (2,1,-1).
+\]
+The induced nonzero transitions are
+\[
+-2\longrightarrow\{-1,1\},\qquad
+2\longrightarrow\{-1,1\},
+\]
+while $-1$ and $1$ have no outgoing edges.  Thus no directed cycle is
+reachable from a nonzero vertex.  An unanchored formulation would nevertheless
+admit arbitrarily long zero padding before the nonzero transition.  The main
+article avoids that false equivalence by shifting the chain so that its
+initial exposed coefficient is nonzero.  The test reports the literal marker
+\path{unanchored-chain regression edges=7} only after comparing the full
+edge set above.
+
+\section{Arbitrary-alphabet falsification battery}
+
+The second audit uses the Pisot root of
+$x^3-3x^2+2x-1$, which does not satisfy Condition~F.  It checks coefficient
+bounds $D=2,3$ for both the canonical count recurrence and the nonstandard
+initial values $(1,2,4)$.  For each of twelve adjacent-window cases, the
+script enumerates the body coefficients and integer quotients and verifies
+the conclusion
+\[
+k_{t+1}=0,\qquad e_{t+m}=-k_t
+\]
+at and beyond the audited contraction thresholds.  Testing a
+non-Condition-F system guards against accidentally importing zero
+preservation into the implementation.  The proof in the article uses only
+the Pisot embeddings and the finite algebraic separation.
+
+\section{Reproduction and integrity}
+
+From the article directory, run
+\begin{verbatim}
+python artifacts/verify_fixed_cubic_audit.py
+python artifacts/test_bounded_zero_arbitrary_D.py
+\end{verbatim}
+The expected saved outputs are
+\path{artifacts/fixed_cubic_audit_verification.txt} and
+\path{artifacts/bounded_zero_arbitrary_D_verification.txt}.  File hashes are
+listed in \path{artifacts/SHA256SUMS}; paths are relative to the artifacts
+directory and the checksum file uses LF line endings.
